objective: Configuration and scraping: prometheus.yml global settings, scrape_configs, scrape_interval and timeout, relabel_configs and metric_relabel_configs, and target health
secondaryObjectives: Data model and labels: metric names, labels and the time series they identify, sample values and timestamps, and how cardinality grows

Understanding Prometheus limitations: single-node storage, no long-term durability by default, cardinality, no cross-server queries without federation or remote write, and what remote write and Thanos/Cortex-style systems add

sources.cite: Prometheus documentation, Configuration (prometheus.io/docs/operating/configuration and the 2.55 page)
sources.note: Read 2026-11-17 with WebFetch (a summarizing fetch) of the primary page, found by WebSearch. Confirms: scrape_timeout defaults to 10s and cannot be greater than the scrape interval; the relabel action keep drops targets whose concatenated source labels do not match the regex; labeldrop removes matching labels; metric_relabel_configs applies to samples as the last step before ingestion, for example to exclude series too expensive to ingest (relabeling details read on https://prometheus.io/docs/prometheus/2.55/configuration/configuration/).

sources.cite: Prometheus documentation, Metric and label naming
sources.note: Read 2026-11-17 with WebFetch (a summarizing fetch) of the primary page, found by WebSearch. Confirms: use base units such as seconds, with a plural unit suffix; accumulating counts end in _total; never use labels for high-cardinality values such as user IDs, because every label-value combination is a new time series.

The company, the services, the metrics and the people are fictional. The minutes or days each step takes and the effects of each decision are teaching simplifications for exam practice, not measured values.

brief.situation: You run monitoring at Fernhill Logistics, a fictional parcel carrier. After a config change at 09:40 the dashboards for every Kubernetes service went blank. Separately, Prometheus memory has doubled this week and it restarted twice.
handover: The change added a relabel rule to the kubernetes-pods job 'to keep only annotated Pods'.
A new release of the tracking API added a tracking_number label to its request counter.
howItWorks: The terminal shows each command's output; the map shows each component and its status in words.
Move on a check-in at a time. A decision comes to you at each check-in; before the first, you can read the evidence.
At the end you write the record and a short reflection.

then.log: Check-in 2: after a node rotation, half the static IPs belong to other Pods; dashboards show the wrong services' numbers.

labelPrompt.title: Two million series
labelPrompt.context: Each tracking number creates new series.

timingPrompt.title: Timeouts on large nodes
timingPrompt.context: Large nodes take 12 seconds to answer; the job has scrape_interval 15s and scrape_timeout 10s.

choices.label: Set scrape_interval 30s and scrape_timeout 20s for that job, and disable the expensive collectors the dashboards don't use

effects.log: The job scrapes every 30 s with 20 s to answer; fewer collectors run.

choices.feedback: The timeout must be no longer than the interval; trimming collectors makes scrapes cheaper.

choices.label: Silence the flapping alerts for those nodes
choices.feedback: The noise stops, and so does monitoring of those nodes whenever a scrape times out.

choices.label: Set scrape_timeout to 60s and keep the 15s interval

scoring.modelReasoning: relabel_configs act on discovered targets before the scrape: a keep rule whose regex matches nothing drops every target, which the targets page's dropped list shows. Each unique label set is a series, so an unbounded label such as a tracking number grows series without limit; metric_relabel_configs can drop it from scraped samples before storage, and the instrumentation should stop emitting it. scrape_timeout may not exceed scrape_interval, and promtool checks a configuration before reload.
